title: Longest Palindromic Substring
oneLinerQuestion: Find the longest substring in a given string that reads the same backward as forward.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: A palindrome reads identically forwards and backwards, which means it displays bilateral symmetry around its center. A naive brute-force approach checks every O(N^2) possible substring for palindrome properties in O(N) time, leading to an O(N^3) runtime. Instead of testing arbitrary slices from the outside in, we can treat each possible character or character pair as a midpoint and expand outward, reducing the search space to O(N^2) without requiring extra memory.

- Step 1: Identify Center Dualities — In any string of length N, there are exactly 2N - 1 potential centers. An odd-length palindrome centers on a single character (e.g., 'aba' centered at 'b'), while an even-length palindrome centers between two adjacent characters (e.g., 'abba' centered between 'b' and 'b').

- Step 2: Main Traversal Loop — We iterate through the string using an index 'i' from 0 to N - 1. For each position 'i', we evaluate two expansion possibilities: expandAroundCenter(i, i) for odd-length candidates and expandAroundCenter(i, i + 1) for even-length candidates.

- Step 3: Outward Boundary Expansion — Inside the expansion helper, we start with pointers 'left' and 'right' at the chosen center. While the boundary condition (left >= 0 && right < s.length) holds and the characters match (s[left] === s[right]), we decrement 'left--' and increment 'right++' simultaneously to verify progressively larger symmetrical boundaries.

- Step 4: Window Tracking & Maximum Length — Once a character mismatch occurs or an edge of the string is reached, the valid palindrome span is established between (left + 1) and (right - 1). The length of this palindrome is (right - left - 1). If this exceeds our globally tracked maximum length, we record the new maximum and its starting offset: start = left + 1.

- Step 5: Substring Extraction — After all 2N - 1 centers have been explored, the longest palindromic substring is extracted from the recorded start index with length 'maxLength' and returned.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N^2) because expanding from each of the 2N - 1 centers takes at most O(N) comparisons. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space since the algorithm operates in place using pointer arithmetic without additional arrays or lookup tables.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION longestPalindrome(s):
    res = ''
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        p1 = expandAroundCenter(s, i, i)
        p2 = expandAroundCenter(s, i, i + 1)
        IF LENGTH(p1) > LENGTH(res) THEN res = p1
        IF LENGTH(p2) > LENGTH(res) THEN res = p2
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION expandAroundCenter(s, l, r):
    WHILE l >= 0 AND r < LENGTH(s) AND s[l] == s[r] DO:
        l = l - 1, r = r + 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN SUBSTRING(s, l + 1, r)
END FUNCTION
